title: Kripke completeness for intuitionistic propositions

based_on.title: Intuitionistic Logic (ILLC report PP-2006-25; ESSLLI 2005 lectures)
based_on.pages: Section 3.3 printed pp. 17–19: Definition 10, Lemma 11, Definition 12 and the full IPC part of Theorem 13.

summary: Build one canonical ordered model whose worlds recover exactly the intuitionistic consequences of any set of numbered-atom premises.
abstract: Soundness says that intuitionistic proofs are valid in ordered models of growing information. To prove the converse, we construct worlds from consistent collections of formulas that are closed under deduction and choose a disjunct whenever they contain a disjunction. An enumeration of the formulas extends any unsuccessful deduction to such a world while keeping its conclusion absent. Ordering these worlds by inclusion gives one canonical Kripke model. We prove that forcing in this model is exactly membership, including the cases of implication and primitive negation. This yields completeness for arbitrary premise sets in the fixed language with numbered atoms, finite-premise recovery for semantic consequences, and satisfiability compactness.
